**The Whispering Trees**

In a quiet corner of the world, where the sky meets the earth in a soft embrace, there stands a forest of ancient trees. They are not like the others—tall and proud, their bark etched with stories older than time. The villagers call them the Whispering Trees, for when the wind dances through their leaves, they murmur secrets to those who listen.

Lena, a curious girl with wild curls and a heart full of questions, often sat beneath their branches. She would press her ear to the rough bark, straining to hear the faintest of whispers. The trees spoke of forgotten kingdoms, of lovers who turned into stars, and of storms that carried away entire cities. But their favorite tales were of the future—of things yet to come.

One evening, as the sun dipped below the horizon, painting the sky in hues of gold and violet, Lena heard something different. A single word, carried on the breeze: *"Remember."*

She frowned. "Remember what?" she asked aloud.

The trees rustled, their leaves shivering as if laughing. *"Remember us,"* they seemed to say. *"Remember the stories. Remember the magic."*

Lena didn’t understand then, but years later, when the world had grown louder and the forests thinner, she did. She became a storyteller, weaving the whispers of the trees into tales for children who had never known a world where trees could speak. And though the Whispering Trees were long gone, their voices lived on—in her words, in the wind, in the quiet moments between dreams and waking.

For some things are never truly lost, as long as someone remembers.
